phase: Phase 1: Roster parity that cannot drift silently
summary: Phase 1 Green API surface audit complete. The new `rosterParity(opts)` export from `lib/core.mjs` matches the JSDoc contract documented in `tests/parity.test.mjs` header (inputs: agents / rosterDir / expectedRoster; outputs: ok, agentCount, callableCount, agentCountLabel, callableCountLabel, findings with class/name/expected/actual/path/detail). The legacy `agentParity(agents)` signature is preserved and still returns the documented shape `{ok, agentCount, callableCount, duplicates, missingDescriptions, unmappedModels}` against the live 27-agent / 25-callable roster (`{ok: true, agentCount: 27, callableCount: 25, duplicates: [], missingDescriptions: [], unmappedModels: []}`). Consumer integration is unbroken: `scripts/parity.mjs` resolves `agentParity(agents)` and exits with the expected `1` (Phase 2/3 work — operator-side drift), `extensions/measure-harness/index.ts#doctor` still imports `agentParity` from `../../lib/core.mjs` and reads `parity.ok` (TS import path unchanged). Labeled-integer defense is verified: `agentCountLabel` is exactly `"agent count: 27"` and `callableCountLabel` is exactly `"callable count: 25"`; the A3 probe regex (`/^agent count:\s*(\d+)$/` and symmetric `/^callable count:\s*(\d+)$/`) is anchored and labeled, not vacuous. Fail-closed behavior is verified: an unreadable roster directory reports `{class: 'unreadable_source', path, detail}` with `ok: false`; a malformed frontmatter file reports `{class: 'malformed_agent_file', name, path, detail}` with `ok: false`, and the other valid agents still load (per-file isolation, not abort). EXPECTED_AGENT_COUNT and EXPECTED_CALLABLE_COUNT are removed from `lib/core.mjs` (only a JSDoc comment reference remains). `tests/core.test.mjs` was rewritten to assert the derived 27/25 contract (not a frozen 24/22 snapshot). No A1 silent state transitions were introduced. The new `description_mismatch` finding class is a defensible A3 defense (structured fields, fires on a real disagreement, not a count) — but the JSDoc contract header in `tests/parity.test.mjs` was not updated to include this class, which is a non-blocking documentation drift.

nonblocking_findings.description: The Phase 1 Green implementation introduces a new finding class `description_mismatch` (fires when `expectedRoster[*].description` differs from the live agent's `description`, including the case where the expectedRoster does not track description but the live agent does). This class is NOT enumerated in the JSDoc contract header in `tests/parity.test.mjs` (lines 30-33), which lists only `missing_agent | extra_agent | mode_change | duplicate | missing_description | unreadable_source | malformed_agent_file`. The implementation produces 8 finding classes; the contract documents 7. A future contributor reading the JSDoc will not know `description_mismatch` exists and may treat it as a third-party surprise. Defense: the class is well-named and has structured fields (name, expected, actual), so it is a defensible A3 defense, not class-laundering — but the contract documentation must be updated. The Green author documented this deviation in `phase-1-green.json` (NF-1: new_finding_class_description_mismatch). Phase 2 acceptance should require the JSDoc to be brought in sync with the implementation, or the class removed in favor of a different representation.

At the audited HEAD `9494331`, the live MODEL_MAP does not contain entries for `kimi-for-coding/k3`, `kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding`, `kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, or `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` (7 agents are structurally unmapped). However, `parseAgentFile` still uses the silent passthrough `model: sourceModel ? MODEL_MAP[sourceModel] ?? sourceModel : undefined`, so `agent.sourceModel && !agent.model` is never true and `unmappedModels` is structurally unreachable. `agentParity(agents).unmappedModels` returns `[]` and `parity.ok` is `true` despite the 7 unmapped sourceModels. This is the documented Defect #2 from the spec and is explicitly deferred to Phase 2 (per `phase-1-green.json` handoff). The Phase 1 audit does not flag this as a Phase 1 defect — it is recorded so Phase 2 acceptance knows the predicate is still unreachable and the fix is required.

At audit time, the working tree carries 17 modified files and 4 untracked directories that are unrelated to the Phase 1 Green work (16 agent files, config/model-map.json, measure/tracks.md, plus the three other 2026-08-05 tracks). The Green commit (9494331) excluded all of these per the absolute constraint 'DO NOT commit any unrelated dirty file'. The harness remains functional because `parseAgentFile`'s `?? sourceModel` fallback provides a passthrough; the dirty MODEL_MAP additions (kimi-for-coding/k3, kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding-highspeed) are not loaded into the committed `lib/core.mjs`. Audited HEAD is current at `9494331`; the additional commit `d74471a` (recorded post-Green) only adds `phase-1-green.json` and does not modify any code, so the audit scope is correct.

Phase 1 contract test #9 (A3 probe) requires findings.length >= 2 on the missing-description fixture + BASELINE_EXPECTED. Without the new description_mismatch class, only 1 finding (missing_description for agent-a) is produced and the test fails. The Green addition of description_mismatch is therefore required by the test contract — but the JSDoc contract surface was not updated to recognize it. This is the JSDoc contract drift recorded in NF-1.

Phase 1 contract test #10 (A3 labeled-integer parse) uses /\^agent count:\s*(\d+)\$/ and /\^callable count:\s*(\d+)\$/ — both anchored and labeled. A bare rg -q '[0-9]+' probe would pass even for 'abc123def', but the anchored pattern requires the exact prefix 'agent count:' / 'callable count:' and the suffix end-of-string. The probe is not vacuous.

handoff: Phase 1 review-c-ux-api confirms the API surface is correct and consumers are not broken. Phase 1 acceptance should verify: (1) worktree-snapshot.json exists at the supplied path; (2) tests/parity.test.mjs continues to pass 11/11 at the acceptance commit; (3) tests/core.test.mjs continues to pass 5/5 at the acceptance commit; (4) npm test fails with exactly the four S1 intentional-Red files (agents-snapshot, grammar, manifest, preflight) and no Phase 1 regressions; (5) npm run check exits 0. Phase 1 acceptance does NOT need to verify the description_mismatch JSDoc drift (NF-1) — that is a documentation fix for Phase 2 (or a follow-up Green commit if the orchestrator elects to bring the JSDoc into sync). Phase 1 acceptance does NOT need to verify the unmapped-models reachability (NF-2) — that is Phase 2's contract (Story S2). The `doctor()` function in `extensions/measure-harness/index.ts` continues to consume `agentParity(agents)` unchanged; no TS-side migration is required for Phase 1.
